summary: Janice Dean Willis is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. She studied at Cornell University and Columbia University (Ph.D. under Alex Wayman), also studying under Yeshe Thubten. She held long-term posts at Wesleyan University and Agnes Scott College.

Janice Leoshko is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her doctoral studies under Susan L. Huntington and served as Professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).

Jann Ronis specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under David Germano, Jeffrey Hopkins, and Sonam Tenpa, and held an attested post at the University of Virginia in 2007.

Jared Rhoton was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga and completed his dissertation at Columbia University in 1985 under the supervision of Alex Wayman.

Jarl Charpentier was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University under Karl Ferdinand Johansson and at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He spent his career at Uppsala University, becoming Deputy Professor in 1925 and Professor in 1927.
Jaroslav Průšek was a Czech sinologist. He pursued his higher education at Charles University in Prague from approximately 1924 to 1928.

Jason Birch is an Indologist who earned his B.A. Honours at the University of Sydney and his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at Oxford (2011) and SOAS University of London (2020).

Jason M. Wirth is a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teacher Kosho Itagaki. Around 2005, he was appointed professor of philosophy at Seattle University.
Jason McCombs is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a B.S. from the University of Michigan and a PhD from UCLA under Gregory Schopen in 2014, later serving as a lecturer at UCLA.

Jason Neelis is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. After earning his PhD at the University of Washington under Richard Salomon, he held posts at Ruhr University Bochum, Florida, Washington, and Wilfrid Laurier University.

Jason Protass is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD from Stanford University under John Kieschnick. He has held appointments at Ryukoku University as a visiting researcher and at Academia Sinica as a Fulbright Fellow.

Jay Jasanoff is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard University. He served as professor at the University of California, Berkeley, Harvard University (1970–1978; 1998–), and Cornell University (~1978–1998).

Jay L. Garfield works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. After studying under numerous Tibetan and Western scholars, he held professorships at Hampshire College, Smith College, CIHTS, UMass Amherst, the University of Melbourne, and the National University of Singapore.

Jay M. Bernstein is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh from approximately 1971 to 1975. He held academic posts at the University of Essex (~1975–1996), Vanderbilt University (~1997–2001), and The New School (~2001).

Jay Valentine is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Delaware, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under Kurtis R. Schaeffer.
Jayachamarajendra Wadiyar was a scholar in the fields of philosophy and Indology. He studied under M. H. Krishna at Maharaja's College, Mysore, between approximately 1934 and 1938.

Jayandra Soni is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned doctorates from Banaras Hindu University and McMaster University. He taught Indology and Tibetology at the University of Marburg (1991–2012) and held positions at Innsbruck and the IASS.

Jayashree Sathe is an Indologist and linguist based at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, where she has served as editor-in-chief (attested 2011) and Professor-Editor of the Sanskrit Dictionary (attested 2026).

Jaś Elsner is an art historian and archaeologist educated at Cambridge, Courtauld Institute, and Harvard. His career includes posts at Jesus College, Courtauld Institute, Corpus Christi College, University of Chicago, and as Professor of Late Antique Art at Oxford (2014).
Jean Dantinne was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Étienne Lamotte and held a position as a librarian at the University of Liège.
